suggested_requirements.text: The system shall allow resources to be reviewed before a decision is made whether they should be retained.
The system shall support a workflow to receive and track content, normalize content, validate content, review content, and accept or reject content.
The system shall record a minimal set of identifying information concerning rejection decisions.
The system shall provide a mechanism to eliminate the need to review some resubmissions based on rejection metadata.
The system shall notify producers and donors about rejected content.
The system shall accept content from physical media or via electronic transfer.
The system shall accept content in multiple file formats including TIFF, XML, audio, streaming video, and PDF.
The system shall accept SIPs in XML, MARC, MARC XML, MODS, EAD, DC, and TEI formats.
The system shall accept articles, journals, images, monographs, audio files, video files, websites, numeric data, text files, and databases.
The system shall convert data to accepted file formats as needed.
The system shall prompt a request for resubmission to the Content Originator if an error of transmission or receipt occurs.
The system shall accommodate a resubmitted SIP in case of errors.
The system shall send a configurable automatic system confirmation receipt of SIP to the producer.
The system shall store and track versions of a document, file, or image.
The system shall assign a unique identifier to each object and maintain relationships between parent and child objects.
The system shall keep an audit trail of all actions.
The system shall perform virus checking on SIPs.
The system shall automatically validate the successful transfer of the SIP to a staging area using CRCs or checksums.
The system shall verify the validity of the submission based on submitter, expected format, file quality, duplication, and completeness.
The system shall allow NLM staff to perform manual quality control assurance on staged SIPs via a GUI.
The system shall generate statistical and error reports.
The system shall generate AIPs by transforming SIPs to conform to repository data formatting standards.
The system shall allow entry and validation of additional metadata.
The system shall store metadata in a database in a manner that conforms to repository reformatting and links to corresponding objects via an identifier.
The system shall recognize and document relations among files.
The system shall transfer AIPs to Archival Storage and Descriptive Information to Data Management.
The system shall receive AIPs from Ingest and add them to permanent storage.
The system shall refresh or replace the media on which repository holdings are stored without service interruption.
The system shall provide disaster recovery capabilities including data backup, off-site data storage, and data recovery.
The system shall provide AIPs to Access to generate DIPs.
The system shall maintain the integrity of the Data Management database.
The system shall provide internal validation such as referential integrity of the database contents.
The system shall create and maintain schema or table definitions for Data Management.
The system shall allow creation, maintenance, and access to customized user views of the database.
The system shall generate result sets from query requests.
The system shall support the production of management information reports and statistics.
The system shall allow online updates to individual records by authorized staff.
The system shall audit submissions to ensure they meet repository standards.
The system shall maintain configuration management of system hardware and software.
The system shall track negotiation status, written submission agreements, and schedules.
